title: Donors suspend UNRWA funding over alleged staff role in 7 October attack
body:
On 26 January 2024, UN Secretary-General António Guterres asked the head of the UN Relief and Works Agency for Palestine Refugees, UNRWA, Philippe Lazzarini, to investigate extremely serious allegations that several agency staff took part in the 7 October attacks. Lazzarini said Israeli authorities had provided information about the alleged involvement. He terminated the contracts of the staff named and launched an investigation.

Guterres said staff found to have participated in or abetted the attacks should be fired and referred for potential criminal prosecution. An urgent independent review of UNRWA had already been announced on 17 January. The US State Department said it would temporarily pause new funding pending the investigation. EU foreign policy chief Josep Borrell raised serious concerns and called for full transparency.

Al Jazeera reported on 27 January that at least 10 Western countries, including the United States, Australia, Canada, Italy, Germany, Finland, the Netherlands, Switzerland and the United Kingdom, had suspended or paused funding, while Ireland and Norway said they would continue supporting the agency. Lazzarini urged donors to reconsider, warning that the suspension threatened humanitarian work, particularly in Gaza. He noted that more than two million people in Gaza depend on the agency for lifesaving assistance.
